summary: The skill is rewritten around what the reviewer actually sees: title as headline, rationale as the link, notes as plain text, summary always on screen. Anchors come from git diff -U0 hunk headers. The Agent prompt, the /tabthrough command, and the work-docs restate the same contract. Two small fixes at the end make typecheck and lint pass again.

.tabthrough-guide.json.rationale: The sidecar this walk is written into

steps.title: Writing for what the reviewer sees
steps.rationale: The premise of the rewrite and the four fields it dictates — everything below follows from this block
steps.notes:
The sketch is checked against src/model/sidebar.ts and src/model/view.ts: title falls back to the path, notes are always shown as plain text, summary sits on every step. The old skill called notes markdown and on demand; the sidebar does neither.

Below the sketch, the two tables answer how to write the comments: title names the thought, rationale links it, notes carry only the why that is not in the code, and word count follows significance so normal and low steps stay fast.

steps.title: Line numbers from -U0 hunk headers
steps.rationale: The recipe that stops ranges landing on the wrong lines, and the one limit ranges cannot cross
steps.notes:
@@ -a,b +c,d @@ gives new-side lines c..c+d-1 directly; d = 0 marks a deletion that needs side old.

A contiguous run of changed lines is atomic and a one-line gap still joins two runs, so the guide must not aim two steps at one run — this very walk hit that on the block above.
